messages:
Lina (People Ops): Quick update: calibration logistics are finalized. Self-reflections close 2026-05-12 23:59 PT. Managers need to complete their summaries by 2026-05-19. Calibration panels run 2026-05-24 -> 2026-05-26. Final ratings locked 2026-05-28. Please read the anchor doc before panels: https://go/redwood/calibration-anchors :sparkles:

Tom (People Ops): New this cycle: two short pre-reads for each review (public manager summary + anonymized evidence bullets). Prep helps panels move faster. Pre-reads should be uploaded by 8am on the day of the panel.

Kavita (Eng Manager): What do we include in "anonymized evidence bullets"? Examples?

Lina (People Ops): Keep it 2-3 neutral statements of concrete outcomes, e.g.:
- "Reduced end-to-end latency for feature X by 30% measured via prod traces"
- "Led cross-team rollout; took ownership of incident response and postmortem"
Avoid names or team identifiers. No HR-sensitive details.

Ben (IC): Will managers be required to discuss calibration outcomes with direct reports before finalizing comp changes? Last cycle was vague about timing.

Tom (People Ops): Good catch. New policy: managers MUST have a 1:1 with each direct report within 3 business days after ratings are finalized to share the outcome and development plan. Document template: https://go/redwood/manager-1on1-template

Cal (Director): For calibration panels: how are conflicts handled if panel disagrees strongly with manager recommendation?

Lina (People Ops): Process summary:
```
1) Manager proposes rating + written rationale in Manager Summary form.
2) Panel reviews anonymized evidence and votes.
3) If panel majority differs by >1 band, panel lead flags for escalation.
4) People Ops schedules a rapid reconvene with manager + panel lead to align (15-30 min).
5) If unresolved, a calibration appeal goes to the Calibration Chair (Exec sponsor) for final determination.
```
We aim to minimize escalations; panels should surface gaps instead of immediate overrides.

Kavita (Eng Manager): Any guidance on distribution expectations? I want to avoid forced curves but managers ask for targets.

Tom (People Ops): We don't do a forced bell curve. We provide distribution guidelines for planning (historical bands) and encourage evidence-first decisions. The anchor doc includes percentile-based context (e.g., what a "high" band means in impact+scope).

Ben (IC): Is there an appeals window for employees unhappy with their rating?

Lina (People Ops): Yes 0 business days after the rating release employees can submit an appeal. Appeals should provide new evidence or point out procedural issues. People Ops triages and routes appeals to the Calibration Chair.

NotifyBot: Reminder: manager summaries due in 7 days for teams with >3 direct reports. Upload link: https://go/redwood/manager-summary-2026 :bell:

Cal (Director): Can we get a short, paste-ready meeting blurb for managers to invite calibration panel members?

Tom (People Ops): Use this snippet: 

"Subject: Calibration Panel - [Team] 
Please review attached anonymized pre-reads before the session. Bring 1-2 clarifying questions per review. We'll timebox to 10 minutes per person. Link to anchors & checklist: https://go/redwood/calibration-anchors"

Kavita (Eng Manager): Timeboxing is helpful. How strict are we on the 10-min target? Some complex cases need longer.

Lina (People Ops): Default is 10 minutes. If a case is complex, panel can request a 15-minute follow-up slot. Please mark the pre-read "complex" so we can allocate correctly.

Ben (IC): Any change to the self-reflection template? I liked the shorter one last cycle.

Tom (People Ops): Keep using "Self-Reflection (concise) 2026" for all ICs. It asks for: 3 achievements (1 line each), 1 learning, 1 ask for manager support. Managers use "Manager Summary 2026" which includes recommended rating and calibration fields.

Lina (People Ops): Final admin note: if you're traveling during panels, add your availability to the RSVP sheet in the anchors doc and flag any direct reports affected by timezones. We'll try to accommodate by running a late-afternoon panel slot. Thanks!
